answer: Each identity must lock a non-transferable sable bond countersigned by two distinct peers who hold ivory standing and have never attested that address. An attacker with N clones faces quadratic cost because the pool of clean ivory peers shrinks with every alias, requiring unique countersigners and tying N bonds, while an honest agent pays only its single bond. The design fails if peers collude across a shale cut to reuse countersigners.
